12_marg449: Samuel wrote the first book of Kings up to his death; then David; after [him] Solomon; finally the prophets.
12_marg450: Twenty-two letters are found among the Hebrews, according to whose number twenty-two volumes are reckoned among them, among which the book of Kings is held third in order after Judges. Fittingly is Kings placed after Judges: because now there are rulers of the Church, afterwards the kingdom; or because judgment will go before, and everlasting empire will follow.
12_marg451: It is interpreted 'two heights', so that two tribes may be understood, namely the royal and the priestly, from which his father and mother came.
12_marg452: ORIGEN. Or Armathaim, which is found in other codices, is interpreted 'their height'. Sophim, watchtower or rock. Ephraim, fruitfulness. He is said to have dwelt in mount Ephraim and in Ramathaim Sophim, on high, namely in the contemplation of the virtues, so that the loftiness of his mind might not be cast down, nor its unity torn, by any thoughts of vices lying beneath and barking round about. Therefore he is said to be not of the valleys or of the plains, but of mount Ephraim, that is, the fruitful, in which the nobility of all the virtues is known to bear fruit.
12_marg453: He had two wives, of whom the nobler, that is, Anna, was barren, as Sara the nobler wife of Abraham. But the second, that is, Phenenna, was fruitful, as Agar the Egyptian. Elcana, then, who is the possession of God, is made a father first by the second wife, because God had shut up the womb of Anna, which afterwards he opened. Phenenna is interpreted 'conversion', Anna 'grace'. Whoever, then, wishes to be the possession of God, let him have these two wives, and the first the nobler, that is, grace. For she is first joined to a man through faith. Whence: "By the grace of God you are saved through faith." Then let him be joined to Phenenna, that is, to conversion, because after the grace of faith follows amendment of morals. Phenenna first bears sons, because we bring forth our first fruits through conversion; for unless we are turned from evil, we are not made fathers by Anna. The sons of Phenenna do not stand at the altar; yet they are not made empty, because they eat of the divine sacrifices. He, then, who is converted from sin begets from conversion works of justice; and afterwards Anna, that is, the soul, roused by good zeal, prays that she may have sons who stand before God, that is, sons of grace. For he who is free for God "and meditates on his law day and night" is a son of grace. Hence in the Gospel Martha is busy about much serving, fulfilling works of justice, and as it were begets sons of conversion. Mary, sitting at the Lord's feet, hears his word, and chooses the best part, and begets a son of grace, who may say: "But it is good for me to adhere to my God." Anna begets a son Samuel, of whom it is said: "And Samuel among them that call upon his name"; who is called 'there is God himself'; for where the spirit of grace is, there is God. For unless the works of conversion go before, we cannot beget the gifts of the Holy Ghost. Let us pray for this offspring in imitation of Anna, as she herself did.
12_marg454: First the generation of the prophet is to be told historically; then the allegory is to be continued. Elcana, the father of Samuel, was of the stock of Levi, but not of the generation of Aaron the priest. For he was, according to Paralipomenon, the son "of Jeroam, the son of Eliel, the son of Thau, the son of Suph, the son of Elcana, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai, the son of Elcana, the son of Joel, the son of Azarias, the son of Sophonias, the son of Thahath, the son of Asir, the son of Abiasaph, the son of Core, the son of Isaar, the son of Caath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel." His mother too is shown to be of the tribe of Juda from this, that he is called an Ephrathite from Ephrata, the wife of Caleb, who was of the tribe of Juda, not from Ephraim; as David is called the son of an Ephrathite man, that is, of Isai, who was not of Ephraim but of Juda. He, being strong among the citizens of Ephraim [Ephrem], dwelt in the city Ramathaim Sophim, which is in the Thamnitic region near Diospolis, whence was Joseph, who in the Gospel is said to be of Arimathea. And he had two wives, Anna and Phenenna. Fittingly too is the barrenness of Anna mentioned, whose childbearing was the more renowned: as Sara was first barren and Agar the Egyptian bore; and Rachel, for whom Jacob long served, was long barren, while her sister rejoiced in the number of her offspring.
12_marg455: Watchmen, who perhaps are the prophets, whose son is Elcana.
12_marg456: Sophim, heights or watchtower: this is the heavenly Jerusalem, coming from which he taught contemplation and by his death made [us] possess it.

12_interl601: of the height of the virtues
12_marg457: JEROME. He is interpreted 'possession of God', who is called a man by strength of mind, and one: not changeable, not wandering, but firm and unconfused. All too are fittingly called one who have one wisdom, who confess one Jesus Christ, who are filled with one Spirit of God. Whence: "All run indeed, but one receiveth the prize." Each of the foolish is not one but many; whence: 'A fool is changed as the moon.' But God is called one not in number, but because he is never changed. Whence: "But thou art always the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail."
12_marg458: Allegorically: the possession of God, who is the Son of God, saying: "The Lord possessed me"; who is well called one man, not in number, but because he is never changed, nor is God made other than himself.
12_marg462: Suph: pouring out; because, coming to us through mercy, sealed in his passion, he says: "My God, my God," where, emptying himself, he poured himself out. Whence: "Thy name is as oil poured out": poured out from his invisible things to our visible things.
12_interl608: from Ephrata the wife of Caleb, not from Ephraim
12_marg463: Fruitful, because he abounds in the gifts of the Holy Ghost.
12_marg464: From Ephrata the wife of Caleb, or from the city Ephrata, which afterwards was called Bethlehem; or from Ephraim, as some say, because he was of Ramatha, a city of Ephraim, which is situated on mount Sophim, which is a mountain in the tribe of Ephraim.
12_interl609: namely conversion from evil, and grace
12_marg465: AND HE HAD TWO WIVES etc. Phenenna is the Synagogue, which, fruitful at first, bore sons to God through the law, but now because of unbelief remains unfruitful. Anna, the barren one, is the Church of the Gentiles, which, once barren of spiritual offspring, now redeemed by the grace of Christ (for Anna is interpreted grace), bears sons to God through baptism and the Holy Ghost.

12_interl614: that the more desired, the more welcome the birth might be

12_marg468: PHINEES, a mute mouth, signifies the scribes and Pharisees, who are called sons of Heli because Heli bears the type of the priesthood. They, because they did not receive him whom the law and the prophets foretold, turned to the madness of unbelief, deserved to have a mouth mute from the confession of Christ. And because they would not raise up the seed of faith to Christ, their dead brother, they deserved to be unshod and to be outside the lot of those of whom it is said: "Your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace." And because they tried to claim the name of bridegroom for themselves, not for Christ, usurping the Church, they remained stripped of all dignity, unshod of the examples of the patriarchs and prophets. Whence Silo, where the priests were, is interpreted 'his dismissal' or 'petition', because they petitioned Pilate to release Barabbas to them. Deservedly, then, were they dismissed and forsaken by God.
12_interl623: because after the victims were offered the Levite ate with his wives and sons and daughters
12_marg469: That is, garments, which they changed at the festivals. But to Anna he gave one portion, sorrowful, because she had no sons to whom he might give more.
12_marg470: That is, to the Synagogue and her sons he gave portions, that is, temporal goods, according to that: He gave them the lands of the Gentiles; and because the words of God were first committed to them. To Anna, that is, to the Church of the Gentiles, he gave one portion, namely among the Gentiles [so the edition: "ingentium"]. Well does it say sorrowful, because the Lord had shut up her womb; for the time of having mercy on her had not yet come, that she should be made fruitful by spiritual grace. As Phenenna despised Anna, so the Synagogue despised the Gentile world. Many of the Gentiles awaited the coming of the Redeemer, as we find in Job; and because they persevered in prayer, at last the Redeemer brought consolation to Anna weeping and not taking food, saying: Anna, why weepest thou? etc. Better to the Church is her husband, that is, Christ, than the ten sons whom the Synagogue brought forth to God; because she sometimes loves Christ more, that is, his grace, than those whom she bore carnally.
12_marg471: Elcana is the preacher whom the Lord possesses; Phenenna and Anna the active and the contemplative life. Phenenna, fruitful in sons and daughters, is the active, begetting strong works and weak ones. Phenenna is interpreted 'conversion', because the active life must turn itself with care to the actions by which it may profit its neighbours. For the active life is to give bodily bread, or [the bread] of doctrine, to the hungry; to correct the erring; to call back the proud to the way of humility; to take care of the sick; to dispense to each what is fitting. Anna is interpreted 'grace', because contemplation is had through grace. She is barren because, since no one can penetrate it as it is, and no one suffices to preach what he perceives in it, it comes about that no one begets many sons by preaching it. The contemplative life is to hold fast the love of God and neighbour with the whole mind, to rest from outward action, to cleave to the desire of the Creator alone, so that it now pleases one to do nothing. Whoever wishes to be made the possession of God, let him take these two wives: the active first, the contemplative afterwards. Especially let the teacher pass from the embraces of Phenenna to the embraces of Anna, and give portions to each, joining virtues to virtues.

12_marg472: HOW LONG [WILT THOU BE] DRUNK etc. Man seeth the face, God the heart. Heli, who looked only at her mouth, thought her drunk. But the Lord, who saw her heart, had regard to her prayer. And here a form of praying is handed down to us: that we should pray not in much speaking but in compunction of heart and the shedding of tears; because: "A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: a contrite heart" etc.

12_marg474: For the Church was by no means changed from faith and love of the Redeemer by turning aside to other ways.
12_marg475: RABANUS. Because Anna devoutly asked of the Lord, she conceived and bore. So the Church, praying through natural understanding, conceived the mystery of the Incarnation in the heart and brought it forth by the mouth of confession.
12_marg476: RABANUS. Samuel: 'petition of God' or 'his name is God'; because [God was] the author, namely, of his birth, because to the barren woman praying he granted a son, who should serve him in the temple all his days.
12_marg477: That is, God; Anna's firstborn, a prophet. Who is this but the Lord's man?
12_marg478: ANNA BORE A SON: that is, the Church from the nations first nourished with milk the son whom she conceived through faith, that is, by simple understanding, in her hearers. The three calves signify the three times in which the Church awaited Christ. The three bushels of flour are faith, hope and charity, which the Church offered; or the three sons of Noe, from whom the Church offered many to God through faith. These gifts the Church of the Gentiles offers for the child, to show that she has borne the child, that is, has received the faith of Christ and wishes to show it by works. And she brought him to Silo, into the house of the Lord, when with perfect faith in the incarnation she joined herself to the primitive Church from the Jews.
12_marg479: What thou hast willed; or his [word], which he promised through Heli when he said: God grant thee thy petition etc.
12_marg480: SO THE WOMAN STAYED etc. Anna will not bring the child to the house of God before he is weaned; because the Church advances no one to the priesthood while he shares the milk of infancy and is not capable of solid food and spiritual understanding.

12_marg482: [The bottle] which holds three bushels. It is not understood that she offered all these to God at once, but some to God, some to the priest, that he might gladly receive the child into the ministry.

And this tenth part was a tenth of an ephi; whence it is understood that Elcana did not offer three bushels of flour with three calves, but nine tenths.

12_marg484: She is not found praying in this canticle except in two phrases only. One is where she says: "I have joyed in thy salvation." The other there: "For there is no other [God] besides thee." But the just man prays without ceasing, because he does not cease to do well. Whence: "The lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice." He lifts up his hands who lifts up his deeds. When Moses lifted up his hands Israel overcame, but when he let them down Amalec overcame; because while the servant of God lifts up his deeds the people of God overcomes, but if he lets them down Amalec, the enemy of God, overcomes.

12_marg486: The kingdom of the Church, because it rises above the adversities of the world and the desires of the flesh, as a horn rises beyond the flesh.
12_marg487: MY MOUTH IS ENLARGED etc. The mouth of the Church is the preachers, whose teaching is enlarged over the enemies, because it surpassed the knowledge of the scribes and Pharisees.
12_marg488: MY MOUTH IS ENLARGED etc. RABANUS. AUGUSTINE. Because the word of God is not bound: not bound in pressures, not bound in its heralds.
12_marg489: RABANUS. AUGUSTINE. [In] Christ, whom the old man Simeon embraces as a child and knows as great, saying: "Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word in peace," because: "My eyes have seen thy salvation." If I shall have joyed in the salvation of God, then my mouth shall be enlarged: namely, through meditation on the word of God one comes to the lifting up of the heart. Whence: "Our mouth is open to you, O ye Corinthians, our heart is enlarged." From the breadth of the heart wisdom is ministered to the mouth.

12_marg490: THERE IS NONE HOLY etc. ORIGEN. Besides thee, O Lord, because no one is made [holy] except by thee; although there be that are called many gods and many lords, yet none of them is by nature that which God is, because he alone is he who says: I am who am. For a shadow, in comparison with a body, is not; or smoke, in comparison with fire.
12_marg491: RABANUS. AUGUSTINE. He does not say 'none but the Lord', but none is as the Lord, holy and sanctifying, just and justifying.
12_marg492: DO NOT MULTIPLY etc. She rebukes the Jews and the wise of the world, who exalt themselves against the knowledge of God.

12_marg494: Things which pertain to the old man, that is, to carnal conversation. Seek knowledge, which is not but from God, because he is the Lord of knowledge: "In whom are all the treasures of wisdom."
12_marg495: RABANUS. AUGUSTINE. He knows you even where no one knows. Whence: "For if any man think himself to be something, whereas he is nothing, he deceiveth himself." These things are said to the adversaries of the city of God, belonging to Babylon, trusting in their own strength; of whom are the Jews, who, not knowing the justice of God, that is, that which God gives to man, who alone is just and justifying, and seeking to establish their own, as though prepared for themselves from themselves, not imparted by the Lord, have not submitted themselves to the justice of God. But the God of knowledge and judge of consciences sees the thoughts of men, that they are vain; vain because they are properly men's, and are not from him from whom men are.
12_marg496: Because he withdraws himself from thoughts which are without understanding; or, to him are thoughts prepared, that is, made manifest. Whence: "The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men."

12_marg497: THE BOW OF THE MIGHTY. RABANUS. AUGUSTINE. That is, the intent of those who seem to themselves so powerful that without God's help they can fulfil the divine commandments.
12_marg498: AND THE WEAK. RABANUS. AUGUSTINE. Those who trust in the mercy of God say: Have mercy on me, O God, for I am weak. The Gentile people was weak when it was a stranger to the testament of God; but now it is girt with strength, since, clothed with the shield of faith and the helmet of salvation and the sword of the spirit, it will be able to extinguish the fiery darts of the devil.
12_marg499: The Jews, filled before, namely with the mysteries of the [divine] words, have hired themselves out for bread, that is, have separated themselves from God, or have torn themselves from their own seats, lest they should receive the gospel which treats of the bread that came down from heaven.
12_marg500: The filled are the same as the mighty, that is, the Israelites, to whom were committed the words of God; but the sons of the handmaid were diminished, who withdrew themselves and did not believe in the Saviour, and in those very breads, that is, the divine words, perceived only earthly things. But the Gentiles, to whom the law was not given, after they came through the New Testament to those words, by hungering much passed over the earth, because in them they savoured not earthly but heavenly things. In the Greek: thus those full of bread were diminished, and the hungry passed over the earth.
12_marg501: and the hungry are filled: that is, the Gentiles, formerly in want, now taste the bread of the word of God, for it is sweet. They were fed with the knowledge of God until the barren bore many: in the Hebrew sabba, which signifies seven and many.
12_interl659: it is the cause why it was so done
12_marg502: In the number seven the universality of the Church is designated; whence John too writes to seven Churches, showing that he writes to the fulness of one. Whence: "Wisdom hath built herself a house, she hath hewn her out seven pillars." The Church was barren among the Gentiles before this offspring which we behold arose. We behold too the earthly Jerusalem, formerly fruitful, now weakened; because whatever sons were in her were free by her strength [so the edition]; but now, because the letter is there and the spirit is not, having lost her strength she is weakened.
12_marg503: RABANUS. For many, in the Hebrew and in the Seventy is found: seven. The Jews say that when Samuel was born the firstborn son of Phenenna died, and, as each son was born to Anna, a son of Phenenna died. But Phenenna had seven; Anna, however, five. 12_marg504: He killeth and maketh alive the barren, or the same [people]; which he repeats, adding: he bringeth down to hell and bringeth back again. Whence: "If you be dead with Christ, seek the things that are above." They are killed unto salvation to whom it is said: "Mind the things that are above, not the things that are upon the earth," as are, namely, those who, hungering, passed over the earth. "For you are dead," he says, unto salvation, namely, "and your life is hid with Christ in God." The same, then, are made alive, or living, as Christ "was delivered up for our sins, and rose again for our justification." And because he says: Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell: God brought the same down to hell and brought him back. By this his poverty we are made rich.

12_marg512: That [the Greek says] he will make his adversary weak can also be understood, from the ambiguous Greek, as his own adversary. For when the Lord begins to possess us, our adversary becomes his, and is overcome by us, not by our strength, because not in his own strength is a man mighty.
12_marg513: SHALL FEAR THE LORD etc. The adversaries are the Jews, upon whom the Lord thundered in the heavens, that is, in the apostles, when he terrified them by threatening hell, confirming the threats with signs; whence many were converted. Or they shall fear in the judgment him whom, opposing him here, they despised; upon whom he will thunder, saying: 'Depart into everlasting fire'; and lest this befall all, the Lord daily thunders in the heavens, that is, in the Scriptures and the teachers.
12_marg514: RABANUS. Because the just retribution will be in the day of judgment; but meanwhile he thunders from his clouds, which he filled with the Holy Ghost after he ascended into heaven.

12_marg515: Man's last things: because the things that are changed for better or for worse in the middle time will not be judged, but the last state in which he shall have been found.
12_marg516: That is, to Christ. Empire, that is, the Church. Whence: "I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance." Or empire, that is, the power of judging, because: "He hath given all judgment to the Son."
12_marg517: RABANUS. The Christian people, to whom he gives the power of ruling the flesh, that in it he may overcome the world, who for its sake shed his blood.

12_marg518: Of the Christian people anointed with chrism; yet the whole body with its head is one Christ. This Anna prophesied, the mother of Samuel, in whom was then figured the change of the old priesthood, and now fulfilled, when the fruitful was weakened, that the barren might have a new priesthood in Christ.
12_marg519: HELI is interpreted 'stranger'. For he is a stranger to God who does not correct those subject to him. Ophni, 'infamy of conversion'; and deservedly is he so called who puts off being converted to better things. Phinees, 'stopping of the mouth' or 'sparing the mouth'. We read of two priests Phinees: one just, the son of Eleazar; the other unjust, the son of Heli. Priests who guard their mouth, lest anything perverse come forth from it, are signified in the son of Eleazar. But those who have a mouth stopped, either by unskilfulness or by consciousness of sins, are figured in the son of Heli.
12_marg520: Josephus relates that the priest Heli had two sons, Ophni and Phinees, injurious toward men and impious toward the divinity, and they spared no iniquity: some gifts from those who offered they set apart for themselves on account of [their] honour, others they took by way of plunder; they offered insults to the women who came together for religion's sake, doing violence to some, persuading others with gifts; and their life differed in nothing from the worst tyranny. Whence Heli too was condemned for their iniquity, because he punished them with too little severity of correction; although indeed he restrained and rebuked them with gentleness, yet with the mildness of a father, not with the severity and authority of a high priest. Let priests learn, then, that they will be punished for the crimes of the people, and the fault of those under them will be imputed to them.

12_marg521: The coat which Anna, that is, grace, made and gave to the child is the beginning teaching, by which the faithful receive their first rudiments. Whence: "I gave you milk to drink, not meat." But the linen superhumeral signifies chastity and continence with good works. For he who desires to minister to the Lord must live chastely and continently and exercise himself in good works.
12_marg522: IF ONE MAN SHALL SIN etc. One does not sin against a man in the same way as one sins against God; because to sin against a man, that is, against a neighbour, is lighter and more venial. But to sin against God, that is, to withdraw from his worship, is the sin of impiety, which is more hardly punished and more slowly forgiven. And when one sins against a man, by appeasing the man he makes God placable to himself. But when one sins against God, who shall pray for him? That is, through whom shall he make God propitious to himself? Not that no pardon is to be hoped for by those who sin in the divine office; but greater is the punishment and slower the pardon for those who offend in things consecrated to God than if they had hurt their neighbour by word or deed, because the greater the glory, the heavier the offence.

12_interl700: the dignity and strength of the priesthood
12_marg523: Aaron, namely. For who else was in the Egyptian bondage who after the deliverance was chosen for the priesthood? For whoever is of his race, when he sees the priesthood of the Christians flourishing throughout the world, but taken away from himself, wastes away with grief and sorrow.
12_marg524: RABANUS. The rival of the house of Heli was Sadoc the priest, who received the priesthood when Abiathar was cast out by Solomon. Whence: "Solomon cast out Abiathar from being the priest of the Lord, that the word of the Lord might be fulfilled, which he spoke concerning the house of Heli."
12_marg525: RABANUS. AUGUSTINE. That, namely, there may always be one of the house of Heli in the house of the Lord, who, seeing another put in the dignity of the priesthood and himself put out, may faint in mind and waste away. But this change of the priesthood, which was figured by Samuel, was fully completed in Christ. For after Samuel there were priests of the race of Aaron, Sadoc and Abiathar and others, up to the time of Christ.
12_interl704: this was fulfilled when Saul commanded the priests of his stock to be slain
12_interl705: either by unbelief or by the sword of Titus
12_interl706: of the change of the priesthood; for the death of the sons signifies the death not of a man but of the priesthood
12_interl708: whence: "I do always the things that please him"
12_marg526: AND MY SOUL. RABANUS. AUGUSTINE. God has no soul, but he is said tropically to have a soul, as hands and feet and the other members of the body. Now it can be said of Samuel that he obeyed God in all things. But Christ pleased God the Father in all things. Whence: "I do always the things that please him"; for whom the Father built a house, which house are we, if we hold fast the confidence and grace and glory of hope unto the end. But it cannot be said of Samuel that a faithful house was built for him, to walk all days before the Lord's anointed, that is, Samuel, since we read in what follows that his sons turned aside after avarice; unless perhaps we take his house to be the Jewish people, which served the Lord all the days of his priesthood. Whence: "And all the house of Israel rested following the Lord."
12_interl709: the Church, or the heavenly Jerusalem
12_marg527: IT SHALL COME TO PASS. RABANUS. This is not said properly of the house of Heli but of the house of Aaron, of whose race even to this day they come and are converted.
12_interl714: the saving sacrifice, carnal things being cast off
12_interl715: that is, the people itself, mighty with Christ as priest. Whence: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood" etc.
12_marg528: A MORSEL OF BREAD. RABANUS. "The bread that I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world." Because he had said that he gave food to the house of Aaron from the victims of the Old Testament, which were the sacrifices of the Jews, he says that a morsel of bread must be asked for, to eat; which is the sacrifice of the Christians and the food of souls.
12_marg529: PRECIOUS. RABANUS. Rare. Whence: In those days there was no manifest vision; for because of the sins of the people and of the prelates the Lord did not appear through visions or through angelic answers, as he appeared to the fathers.
12_marg530: THE LAMP. RABANUS. Which burned in the tabernacle before the light of day. For at daylight it was put out, but it gave light until morning. Or this signifies that Heli would remain in blindness until he was utterly put out with his offspring, that is, died. But mystically the blindness of Heli signifies the blindness of the Jews, who did not acknowledge the Saviour present, nor the brightness of his miracles, nor his teaching, until the priesthood was overthrown with the people and the temple.
12_interl717: it can be understood by the threefold calling, because he was to be prophet, leader and priest
12_interl718: because the divine word, the mystery of prophecy, had not been revealed to him
12_marg531: [BOTH HIS EARS] SHALL TINGLE etc. RABANUS. It is the threat of God upon Heli and upon his house, because, namely, for the sin of the sons of Heli the house was deprived of the priesthood of the Lord. Whence: The ears of the hearers shall tingle with vehement amazement.
12_marg532: It was a proverb among the Hebrews. And the sense is: if thou hide from me, may the evil which the Lord hath spoken to thee concerning me come upon thy head.
12_marg533: AND NOT ONE [OF HIS WORDS] FELL. RABANUS. Because nothing of the things which the Lord spoke was void. For empty words fall to the ground, to be held as nothing and trodden under foot in the contempt of all. Whence Job: "The light of my countenance fell not to the earth"; because he had been accustomed to hold his countenance in such gravity that it was not loosened by contemptible mirth. But whenever he showed himself cheerful to those present, he did it for a certain reason of their profit.
12_marg534: FROM DAN TO BERSABEE. RABANUS. JEROME. By the boundaries of Judea he takes in the whole of the people. Dan is a little village at the fourth milestone from Paneas, which is so called to this day; the boundary of the province of Judea toward the north, from which the Jordan, breaking forth, took its name from the place. For the Hebrews call a river or stream Ior. Dan is interpreted 'judgment' or 'judging'. Bersabee, in the tribe of Juda or of Simeon, is a large village at the twentieth milestone from Hebron, lying toward the south, in which a garrison of the Romans is stationed; from which the boundaries of Judea, beginning, stretch as far as Dan. Nor should anyone wonder if he finds cities of Juda in the tribe of Simeon or of Benjamin. For the tribe of Juda, strong and warlike, often overcoming its adversaries, held the princedom among all the tribes. Therefore the lots of other tribes are counted in its portion. Otherwise, Scripture shows that Simeon dwelt in the midst of the tribe of Juda.
12_marg535: ISRAEL: a man seeing God, or strong with God; these are the believers. The Philistines, falling with drink: namely the demons, who, made drunk with the cups of pride, have themselves fallen and hasten to pervert men. Against them Israel, that is, the faithful, lest they yield, but that they may overcome, encamp by the stone of help, that is, the law of Christ, where the stone, that is, Christ, is found, of whom: "The stone which the builders rejected." But while the faithful meditate on the law of the Lord that they may find him their helper, the Philistines come into Aphec, that is, new fury: then, because the unclean spirits see the faithful press more on the divine laws, they therefore contrive sharper and new combats; whence those who trust in their own strength and glory in human wisdom, and through this despise the grace of the gospel, the unclean spirits easily lay low, as it were four thousand.
12_interl721: a man seeing God, or strong with God
12_marg536: BY THE STONE OF HELP. The stone of help, which Samuel afterwards set up as a sign, when the Lord first helped him.
12_marg537: APHEC. RABANUS. JEROME. It is a place near the village of Esrom, of the city of Jezrael, where Saul fought, in the lot of Aser; and it is interpreted new fury, or seizing; for those who deserved the wrath of the Lord were seized by the enemies.
12_marg538: The children of Israel brought the ark where it was taken. And the faithful from the Jews carried the two testaments over to the Gentiles.
12_marg539: For there was a table upon the ark, which the cherubims covered with their wings, where the Lord appeared through an angel and spoke. Cherubim is the fulness of knowledge, which is found in Christ and in the two testaments.
12_marg540: The great shout is the voice of the preachers, strengthened by miracles, brought forth from the two testaments; and the earth rang with the voice of the preaching, the wise of the world; the demons too groaned, believing that they were overcome.
12_marg541: The Jews worship one God, but the Gentiles speak after their own fashion.
12_marg542: AND THE ARK OF GOD WAS TAKEN. The ark taken by the foreigners signifies that the testament would pass over to the Gentiles.
12_marg543: AND WHEN HE HAD NAMED THE ARK OF GOD. RABANUS. Josephus relates these things thus: when Heli heard that the ark had been taken by the enemies, troubled with grief, falling from his seat he died, having lived ninety-eight years, of which he held the princedom forty. On that day the wife of Phinees his son died, since she could not bear to live after the fall of her husband. And she bore a son of seven months, whom they called Ichabod, that is, inglorious, because at that time such a misfortune had befallen.
12_marg544: Heli was the first to hold the princedom from the house of Ithamar, the son of Aaron. For before, the priests were of the house of Eleazar, from whom the son received the honour from the father; and Eleazar handed it to Phinees his son. After him Abiezer his son received the honour, which he left to Bozi his son, whom Ozi his son succeeded; and after him Heli held the priesthood; [afterwards] those of the house of Eleazar received it again.
12_interl724: whoever turns backward from faith and truth must fall and die. But mystically, when the ark of the Lord passed over to the Gentiles, the priesthood of the Jews perished.
12_marg545: And when Heli falls from his seat, the seat of the high priest remains empty, and the glory of the priests is put out.
12_marg546: Heli dies, the sons die too, because the high priesthood fails with the old priesthood.
12_marg547: The wife of the priest did not die before she bore a male child; nor did the Synagogue wholly perish before the primitive Church, which was from it, believed.
12_marg548: AND WHEN SHE WAS UPON THE POINT OF DEATH etc. By an evident sign it is figured that, when the carnal priesthood of the Jews was put out, the carnal Synagogue, which clung carnally to it, is put out.
12_marg549: The believers console the Synagogue, but she, despairing, gives no heed, and reckons the new offspring not to glory but to ignominy. Whence it follows: and she called the child Ichabod. Chabod: glory; Ichabod: the glory has fallen. For the glory was carried away when the ark was taken. Whence: "The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof."
12_marg550: INTO AZOTUS. RABANUS. Which is also Asdod, one of the five cities of the Palestinians, assigned indeed to the tribe of Juda but not held, because it could not drive out the natives. And it is interpreted 'fire of the father' or 'burning'. And well is the place so called where the idol Dagon was, because the coming of the ark into Azotus was the burning of the devil, the father of all enemies or of the wicked. Dagon, which is interpreted 'fish of sadness', signifies the devil, who in the sea of this world devours sinners, who in Job also is named Leviathan and Behemoth.
12_marg551: It is the place in which Samuel set up the stone, as is shown in what follows.
12_interl725: after the testament of God came to the Gentiles, at once the idols fell down
12_interl726: there were many defenders of idolatry
12_marg552: The pride of the devil, which is the beginning of all sin.
12_interl727: that is, the faith by which idolatry is destroyed
12_marg553: UPON THE THRESHOLD. RABANUS. It signifies the end fixed beforehand, in which idolatry would cease. For the threshold is the end of a journey.
12_marg554: They found only the back, all the members being broken, which expresses the flight of idolatry. For he who flees gives his back to the pursuer. Whence: "For thou shalt make them turn their back" etc.
12_interl728: out of reverence for their god
12_marg555: AND SMOTE THEM IN THE MORE SECRET PART OF THE BUTTOCKS. Those who receive the testament of God and love the hinder things of this life will justly be tormented in the hinder parts by those very things, which they ought to esteem as dung. For those who take up the testament of God and, looking back to the hinder things, do not strip themselves of the old vanity, are like those who put the ark of the testament beside their idols. And the old things indeed fall even against their will, because: "All flesh is grass"; but the ark remains for ever, namely the testament of the kingdom of heaven which is to follow, where the word of God is for ever.
12_marg556: LET IT BE CARRIED ABOUT. That if, wherever it goes, the stroke accompanies it, we may know that the plague is from God. Which was done by the will of God through their counsel, that the plague might be common, since the guilt was common.
12_marg557: The inward parts; hence extales, where the plague was.
12_marg558: SEVEN MONTHS. The number seven signifies the whole of time, which runs on by the number of seven days; and it signifies that the testament of God will remain among the Gentiles until the consummation of the world.
12_marg559: FIVE EMERODS etc. RABANUS. The five golden emerods and five mice which the Philistines made after their plague and brought to the ark signified that the carnal, given to the five senses of the body, when they have been chastised by the Lord, acknowledging their own crimes confess that they were justly struck, and, though compelled, are changed for the better. This the five cities of the Philistines well signify: Azotus, Gaza, Ascalon, Geth, Accaron, expressing namely those who follow the acts of the outward man. Gaza is a city of the Hevites, in which the Cappadocians dwelt after the former inhabitants were slain. Among the ancients it was the boundary of the Chanaanites near Egypt, and it fell to the lot of Juda, but it could not hold it, because the Enacim, that is, the giants of the Allophyli, resisted most strongly. And it is to this day a notable city of Palestine; yet Gaza is said to be destined to be an everlasting heap, because first it was utterly destroyed and another was built in another place. Ascalon, a noble city of Palestine, was assigned to the tribe of Juda, but it could not overcome its inhabitants. Geth is now a large village called Gethan. Between Antipatris and Thamna there is also another town of this name. Accaron is in the tribe of Dan or in the tribe of Juda, on the left of the Chanaanites, but it did not drive out the former inhabitants; and to this day a large village is called Accaron, between Azotus and Thamna, facing the east. Some think Accaron is the Tower of Strato, afterwards called Caesarea. Azotus is interpreted 'fire of my father' or 'burning'; Gaza 'strength'; Ascalon 'infamous fire' or 'ignoble fire'; Geth 'winepress'; Accaron 'teaching of sadness' or 'of barrenness'. For every concupiscence, infamous and ignoble, inflamed by the devil, urged on by the contrary powers, and pressed out by the winepress of wickedness, pours forth the wine of bitterness in perverse teaching and wicked working. And therefore it tends to death, where there is true sadness and perpetual barrenness.
12_marg560: The cart is the cross of Christ; the ark, sacred Scripture.
12_marg561: TWO KINE. ISIDORE. The kine bearing the ark signify the saints who renounce the world, who have drawn no yoke of sin. For as the kine did not turn aside from the straight way through affection for their calves, so the holy fathers do not swerve from their good purpose through such affection.
12_interl735: the chariot of God is ten thousandfold
12_marg562: BETHSAMES. RABANUS. It is a priestly city in the tribe of Benjamin, which is shown to this day to those going from Eleutheropolis to Nicopolis, at the tenth milestone toward the east. There is another Bethsames in the tribe of Nephthali, in which the old inhabitants remained.
12_marg563: THAT LEADETH. RABANUS. Going, namely, by the king's way to Bethsames, that is, into the house of the sun, namely the heavenly Jerusalem, where the sun of justice ever shines.
12_marg564: AND TURNED NOT ASIDE. RABANUS. That is, they were neither lifted up by prosperity nor broken by adversity. If, then, we tend toward the dwelling of the eternal sun, let us not turn aside from the way of God for carnal affections. But it is to be weighed that the kine of God, set under the cart, go on and low, and yet do not turn their steps from the way. So the preachers of God, and any of the faithful, ought to be within the Church: that they may suffer with their neighbours through charity, and not swerve from the way of God through compassion. For to go to Bethsames with the ark set upon one is to draw near with heavenly knowledge to the dwelling of the inner light. Which we truly do when we do not turn aside for affection for our dear ones. For so ought those to go who, set under the yoke of the sacred law, now carry the ark of the Lord through inward knowledge: that, grieving with the needs of their kin, they do not turn aside from rightness. Whose grace ought so to hold our mind, that it be neither hard if it is not touched by affection, nor, touched too much, slackened into weeping.
12_marg565: BETHSAMES: 'house of the sun'. This is the Church, lighted by the "sun of justice." For the Bethsamites to reap the wheat in the valley is for the teachers of the Church to handle the corn of the word of God in humility. The stone in the field of Josue: Christ in his Church; the wood of the cart: the cross of Christ. To immolate the kine upon the stone is to mortify those converted from the world in the imitation of Christ.
12_interl739: the Levites or the priests, because it was not lawful for others
12_marg566: FOR AZOTUS ONE etc. ISIDORE. The five cities gave five emerods and five mice. But the remaining cities of the provinces, and the towns that were without wall, [gave] mice only. Whence: From the fenced city to the village that was without wall etc.
12_marg567: ABEL. It is a city on the border of Israel, which, called Bethsames before, is now called Abel, either because of the mourning made there over the men of Bethsames, or to distinguish the city from Abel Beth Maacha, from which the wise woman cried out to Joab: They that ask, let them ask in Abela.
12_marg568: BUT HE SLEW. Who, though they were not Levites, dared to look upon the ark. Lest the people should suffer this, in Exodus they stood afar off; Moses alone went up to the Lord.
12_marg569: AND HE SLEW OF THE PEOPLE etc. In the Hebrew: he smote of the people seventy men and fifty thousand men. The seventy men [were] judges, the Hebrews say. It was lawful for no one to see the ark uncovered except the high priest; they were struck, then, because they were unworthy, or had approached unworthily, or had not guarded the ark.
12_interl742: the elders, namely the chief men of the people
12_marg570: AND THEY SENT MESSENGERS. RABANUS. The transfer of the testament of the Lord from the Jews to the Gentiles is signified; because, since they defiled the law with carnal observance and the superstitions of the Pharisees, they refused the teaching of Christ and his disciples. Whence: "To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God: but because you judge yourselves unworthy, behold we turn to the Gentiles."
12_marg571: CARIATHIARIM. RABANUS. It is interpreted town of the woods, of which it is said: "Until I find out a place for the Lord, a tabernacle for the God of Jacob. Behold we have heard of it in Ephrata: we have found it in the fields of the wood." For the place of the Lord is the tabernacle of the breast of the Christian people. For the city of the woods, that is, the assembly of the Gentiles, is a fit place to receive the ark. In the house of Abinadab, which is interpreted 'my father of his own will', and it can say: willingly, namely, to thee.
12_marg572: RABANUS. Cariathiarim is the city of forests, one of the cities of the Gabaonites, belonging to the tribe of Juda, at the ninth milestone for those going from Aelia to Diospolis. From it was Urias the prophet, whom Joakim slew in Jerusalem, as Jeremias writes.
12_interl746: which is interpreted 'my father of his own will'
12_marg573: GABAA. RABANUS. The hill of humble souls. Whence: "Let the mountains receive peace for the people: and the hills justice." The mountains are the greater souls, the hills the lesser. Or again Gabaa is interpreted loftiness, where Eleazar the priest is appointed.
12_marg574: ELEAZAR. RABANUS. 'Help of God'. And well is he who is called by this name chosen to keep the ark of the Lord, because holy men ascribe whatever good they have to God, not to themselves. Whence: "Our sufficiency is from God," who hath made us fit ministers of the new testament.
12_interl747: after the testament abode in the Church, the just were multiplied, who were enlightened by it as days
12_marg575: It was [the twentieth year] when, in the seventh year of Saul's reign, it was brought into the camp from Cariathiarim.
12_marg576: RABANUS. It is not to be understood that the twenty years during which the ark abode in Cariathiarim are to be reckoned up to the eighth year of the reign of David, in which, a great multitude of the people being gathered, he brought it into Jerusalem. For it is found in what follows that in the time of Saul it was taken from this city into the camp against the Philistines; and since it is certain that David brought it into Jerusalem from the house of Abinadab, it remains to be understood that in the days of Saul it was brought back from the camp into the aforesaid city; whence afterwards, in the reign of David, it was brought to Jerusalem. The sense, then, is that from the time the ark abode in Cariathiarim it was the twentieth year when in the time of Saul it was carried into the camp. Or it was the twentieth year when all the house of Israel had rested following the Lord, having cast away their idols and serving him; which Josephus testifies it did through the whole time of Samuel, namely twenty-seven years, and in the first time of the reign of Saul, which, by the same Josephus' testimony, he held twenty years. For when the spirit of the Lord had departed from Saul and an evil spirit drove him to persecute David, some part of the army and of the people followed him.
12_marg577: Astaroth: the making of explorations. He who is a true Israelite puts away from himself every making of the malignant spirits, and boasting and pride, and serves the Lord alone, because there is no fellowship of light with darkness.
12_marg578: It is a city in the tribe of Juda near Cariathiarim.
12_marg579: MASPHATH. RABANUS. Watching, or contemplation, or intent, or the place of judgment. And this place well befits so holy a man, who judged in justice and truth and governed the people with the highest prudence.
12_marg580: RABANUS. The Church, gathered in unity of faith under the new priesthood, drawing the waters of tears, pours them out before the Lord in making satisfaction. The prophet judges the people in Masphath, because the teacher teaches most those whom he has seen to be intent on contemplation and on the love of the heavenly country.
12_marg581: That, as water poured out does not return, so they too should not return to idolatry.
12_marg582: The lamb offered for the people gives the victory to God; and through the passion of Christ, the demons being overcome, peace is given to the faithful.
12_marg583: An innocent life kindled with the fire of charity.
12_interl749: the ears of the Lord [are open] to the prayers of the just
12_marg584: THUNDERED. RABANUS. When the Lord thunders through the preachers of the gospel, the spiritual enemies are turned to flight before Israel, that is, the people of God; and they pursue them as far as the house of knowledge, that is, until all error is purged away and God is truly known.
12_marg585: BETHCHAR. RABANUS. House of knowledge, or house of the lamb.
12_marg586: Another edition: between new Masphath and old, and he called its name Abenezer, or Abongener, that is, stone of help. This is the mediation of the Saviour, through which one must pass from the old Masphath to the new: that is, from the intent by which false happiness is awaited in a carnal kingdom to the intent by which, through the New Testament, true happiness is awaited in the kingdom of heaven, than which nothing is better; thus far God helps.
12_marg587: Masphath: intent. Sen: of teeth. The stone between these: Christ, set between the intent of the Old Testament and the preaching of the gospel; himself a stone because of firmness; of help, because he helps his own when they fight against the demons.
12_marg588: Because those who go beyond these bounds, as the heretics, do not merit the help of God.
12_marg589: AND THERE WAS PEACE. "Christ is our peace, who hath made both one," through whom they who were afar off are made nigh.
12_marg590: It is the city where Josue circumcised the people the second time and celebrated the Pasch, and, when the manna failed, Israel used bread of wheat; where too the stones were carried over from the bed of the Jordan; where the tabernacle of the testimony was for a long time. It fell to the lot of Juda, and to this day the place is shown at the second milestone from Jericho, venerated by the men of that region. But some suppose another Galgal near Bethel.
12_marg591: It is interpreted rolling or revelation. Well, then, did the prophet judge Israel in Bethel and in Galgal and Masphath, and, returning to Ramatha to his house, judged Israel there and built there an altar to the Lord: giving an example that judgment is to be done in the house of God, not indiscreetly or with a malicious mind, but according as Scripture has revealed, and with good intent and brotherly love; and that so we are to return to Ramatha, into our house, that is, to the inward parts of the breast, that we may be free for contemplation and offer on the altar of faith pleasing victims of work and truth.
12_interl755: a lofty sign, or vision of death
12_marg592: The law commanded that an altar not be built except where the Lord had chosen; but lest they should sacrifice to gods he built an altar, in which he is reproved [so the edition].
12_interl756: because, weighed down with age and cares, he could not celebrate the solemnities
12_marg593: HE APPOINTED HIS SONS. RABANUS. Because, according to Josephus, he set one in Bethlehem, the other in Bersabee.
12_marg594: ABIA. RABANUS. The Lord is father, or he was father. Fittingly, then, those who did not persevere in the justice they had begun, and neglected the fatherhood of the Lord, were named 'God was' and 'father was', to signify that they were unworthy of the fatherhood of God.
12_marg595: AND THEY WALKED NOT etc. Because for a gift they oppressed justice, turning aside to feasts and costly banquets.
12_interl758: as if [to say]: worn out by age, thou canst not be over affairs
12_interl760: that is, give testimony to them
12_interl764: which the vines bring forth as the year returns
12_interl766: until God shows what we are to do
12_interl768: hard, or vomiting of a man, or a man vomiting
12_interl774: he had two names; and it was a family belonging to the tribe of Benjamin
12_marg596: Saul, who, God being offended, was made king over Israel, signifies the Jews. For as he became hard and proud and rigid, so as to oppress them with a servile burden rather than free them, so the people of the Jews, though anointed in its priests and kings, was yet a son of the handmaid, who bore unto bondage, and could not attain perfect freedom through the anointing, especially because it would not receive the true and meek king, through whom it could have been freed. Saul, then, is interpreted petition, who was of the stock of Benjamin, because [he was] the son of Cis, the son of Abiel, the son of Seor, the son of Bethoreth, the son of Sared, the son of Aphia. Benjamin: son of the right hand. Cis: hard, or vomiting of a man, or a man vomiting. Abiel: my father God. Seor: little one, or turbulent. Bechoreth: thy firstborn. Sared: descent. Aphia: liberality of the Lord. Israel, then, God's firstborn son, and God his father, was a son of the right hand, because by the help of God he prevailed over his enemies; but because, ungrateful and hard, he went down from the liberality of the Lord, he broke out into blasphemy, and from great became little, and from peaceful turbulent.
12_marg597: RABANUS. That Saul, seeking his father's asses, came to the prophet, by whom he was anointed, signifies that the Jews, following the folly of carnal sense, seek after the luxury of the world through devious errors. For the ass is a brutish and wanton animal. And coming to the prophet, that is, to Moses, they hear that the asses are found, that is, that the goods of the earth are owed to them; by whom also the oil of anointing and the helm of the kingdom are promised, in which for a time they might rescue their brethren from the hand of the enemies.
12_interl776: according to the justice of this life
12_marg598: THERE WAS NOT A GOODLIER. RABANUS. According to the justice of the present life.
12_marg599: RABANUS. This pertains rather to Christ, of whom it is said: "Behold my servant, my elect, whom I have chosen"; and elsewhere: "Who among the sons of God shall be like to God?"
12_interl781: Saul thought that he would not tell of the asses except for a price
12_marg600: A stater is a sicle, which has twenty obols, that is, ten denarii.
12_marg601: Although they resolved to give, we do not read that Samuel received it. Yet if he had received it, it would not be reckoned as the price of divination but as the stipend of a prophet.
12_marg602: NOW IN TIME PAST IN ISRAEL HE SPOKE THUS etc. As Bede says, these are not the words of the historian but of Esdras.
12_marg603: He is called a prophet because through the spirit he foreknows things to come.
12_marg604: THE ASCENT. A clivus is the winding ascent of a mountain.
12_marg605: Saul anointed signifies 'Christ' [that is, the anointed]; who himself too was called Christ; whence: "Why didst thou not fear to put out thy hand against the Lord's anointed?"
12_interl783: that Christ may save his people from the power of the demons
12_marg606: ALL THAT IS IN [THY HEART]. RABANUS. The Hebrews hand down that it was in Saul's heart that he would be king, since he had seen in a vision that he was set on the top of a palm tree, which is the sign of one about to reign.

12_marg619: NAAS, JABES GALAAD. Jabes: sense; Galaad: heap of testimony. Naas, that is, the serpent, namely the devil, goes up against the sense instructed by the testimonies of Scripture.
12_marg620: AND NAAS ANSWERED THEM. The war of Naas signifies the war of the heretics against the Church. Naas is interpreted serpent; Ammon: pressing, or straitening, or people of sorrow; Jabes: dried up; Galaad: heap of testimony. Naas, then, signifies the old serpent, who is the prince of the Ammonites, that is, of the heretics. For this is the people of sorrow, which has not the joy of the Holy Ghost; which arranges a covenant with the people of the Church, that it may pluck out the right eyes, namely the sight of the sound and orthodox faith. It leaves the left eye, that they may perceive only perverse things. But the mind of the faithful, dried from the filth of vices, gathers a heap of testimony, that is, the sentences of holy Scripture, by which it may manfully resist the enemy.

12_marg625: SAUL WAS A CHILD OF ONE YEAR. RABANUS. He speaks by anticipation of Isboseth the son of Saul, of whom it is said in what follows: "Isboseth was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years." But if the whole time in which Samuel and Saul reigned is reckoned from the death of Heli, forty years are found up to the death of Saul. When, then, Saul began to reign, he had a son of one year, who after his father's death reigned two years in Israel, and, slain by robbers, left the kingdom to David.
12_marg626: The time of Samuel is joined with the time and reign of Saul. For the historians could not count him in the number of the judges, since he was a prophet and had not judged the people the whole time of his life, as the others had.

12_marg627: GABAA. It is the city of Phinees the son of Eleazar, where Eleazar himself was buried, and it is interpreted 'hill of the cousin'. Fittingly were three thousand Israelites chosen to fight against the Philistines. For they alone are fit to fight against the enemies of the Church who have perfect faith in the Trinity, in which they may stand above their enemies.
12_marg628: The Philistines are the heretics, who, conspiring with equal consent against the Church, try to lay it waste; to whom some, having forsworn the faith, join themselves, others, while they fear to confess the faith openly, lie hid as it were in caves. The various sects, bound together by one bond of impiety, run about to deceive. The horsemen are those swollen with power who help the heretics. The common people as the sand: the multitude gathered by heretical persuasion. The men remaining with [unclear in the edition: "lavi"]: the catholics cleaving firmly to Christ.

12_marg629: THEY HID THEMSELVES etc. RABANUS. Certain Israelites, namely, having hidden themselves, who had left Saul and the people that was with him, some part of those who are called 'Hebrews', terrified with fear, fell away from Saul and from the men who were with him, and went down into the camp of the Philistines; whence in what follows: But the Hebrews also that had been with the Philistines yesterday and the day before, and had gone up with them in the camp, returned to be with Israel, who were with Saul and Jonathan. All the Israelites also who had hidden themselves in mount Ephraim, hearing that the Philistines had fled, joined themselves with their own in the battle.
12_interl826: Samuel by the Lord's command had bidden him wait for him until he should come to anoint him king, and [that] victims [were] to be offered for seven days, as in the consecration of a priest; and because he did not keep this he is rightly rebuked
12_marg630: THOU HAST DONE FOOLISHLY. RABANUS. It seems to some that Saul sacrificed blamelessly, because Samuel, though waited for according to the agreement, did not come. But he who inquires diligently finds that he was justly blamed and guilty of disobedience. Among the Hebrews it is divided thus: "And thou shalt go down before me to Galgal; for I will come down to thee." Then is added: 'To offer oblations and sacrifice victims of peace, seven days shalt thou wait until I come to thee and show thee what thou art to do.' Samuel, then, did not command that he be waited for seven days, but wished to be waited for seven days to offer oblations and sacrifice victims of peace; which Saul did not do, and therefore he is deservedly blamed and accused of folly.
12_marg631: AND IF THOU HADST NOT DONE THUS etc. AUGUSTINE. It is not to be taken as if the Lord had prepared Saul to reign for ever and then would not keep this for him when he sinned. For he knew that he would sin; but he had prepared his kingdom, in which there should be a figure of the eternal kingdom. Whence he added: And now thy kingdom shall not stand for thee. What was signified in him, then, stood and will stand; but it will not stand for him, because he was not to reign for ever, nor his offspring, so that at least through his posterity, succeeding one another, what was said might seem to be fulfilled: For ever.
12_marg632: BUT THY KINGDOM etc. The rejection of Saul: the taking away of the kingdom of the Jews. David, surviving him: Christ, who would succeed to the people of the Jews.
12_marg633: The man signifies David, or the Mediator of the New Testament himself, who was figured in the chrism with which David and his offspring were anointed.
12_marg634: He sought for himself: not as not knowing where he is, but through a man he speaks after the manner of men, because by so speaking he seeks us. For not only to God the Father but to his Only-begotten himself, "who came to seek that which was lost," we were already so known that "we were chosen in him before the foundation of the world." He will seek for himself, then, it says: [that is,] he will have as his own. Whence in the Latin tongue this verb takes a preposition and is said acquirit, which is clear enough. Even without the preposition quaerere is understood as acquirere, from which gains are called quaestus.
12_marg635: NOW THERE WAS NO SMITH etc. The devil too, through pagans, through heretics, and through false Christians, strives to prevent there being teachers in the Church who may make spiritual arms and give them to us for fighting. For the pagans forbade Christians to be instructed in the liberal arts. The heretics too persuaded princes that the catholic defenders of the Church should be driven into exile, that they might more easily seduce the desolate people. Now too the old enemy turns prelates away from diligence in learning, that he may more easily deceive both them and those under them. The devil is bound by a double guilt: pride, by which he fell, and envy, by which he strives to cast others down. And Philistines is interpreted 'double ruin', Hebrews 'passing over'. "For we have not here a lasting city" etc.

12_marg636: Gift of the dove. These are they who are filled with the gift of the Holy Ghost, through whom the Lord scatters the assemblies of the heretics and turns them to flight. His armourbearer: the disciples of the spiritual, who take their journey not by the plains but by the steeps; because the priests cannot go against the enemies unless, walking by the narrow way between both Testaments, and between prosperity and adversity, as between two rocks on the right and the left, they go forward and climb with the whole effort of the mind to the heights of contemplation. Jonathan does not go over to the enemies unless provoked, because the catholics do not stir up contention against the heretics unless they are first provoked to the combat. Jonathan, then, lays the enemies low in the field of tillage, and the teachers overcome the heretics in meditation on Scripture.
12_interl832: Saul proclaimed a fast, lest, if they ate, the vengeance on the enemies should be delayed
12_marg637: BUT JONATHAN. The gift of the dove: here he signifies those who, having received the grace of the Holy Ghost, prepare to spurn the allurements of the world. For he cannot fight manfully against the spiritual Allophyli, that is, the demons, who does not know how to turn away from the sweetness of the world.

12_marg638: WERE ENLIGHTENED. AUGUSTINE. Not for seeing, for he saw before, but for discerning, because he had touched what was forbidden; whence he was confounded. By which deed everyone who wishes to fight for God is warned to despise all the allurements of pleasures: 'For the lips of a harlot drop honey', that is, carnal pleasure brings forth delight. Of which Jonathan is mystically thought to have tasted, and, caught by the lot, he was scarcely freed by the prayers of the people. Whence it is plain that he who is overcome by the pleasure of the world needs the suffrages of the saints and the prayers of the brethren.

12_marg639: They are said to have sinned against the Lord and to have eaten with the blood because, when the victims were slain, they did not offer the fat and the blood to the priests at the sanctuary according to the law, though they had the sanctuary with them. For when the place of the sanctuary was far off, the blood was commanded to be poured on the ground, namely of those victims which they prepared for their own eating. But when the sanctuary was present, it was poured on the altar of the Lord. Whence in Deuteronomy: "Thou shalt pour the blood of thy victims on the altar: and the flesh thou thyself shalt eat." This the people did not do; therefore it is said: they sinned against the Lord and ate with the blood.
12_marg640: SLAY THEM UPON. That the blood may flow to the ground. Or he ate with the blood because they ate before the evening sacrifice, which after a slaughter it was the custom to make before food. Or they sinned in this, as some hold: that they did not bring their victims to the door of the tabernacle.
12_marg641: AND SLEW THEM. The slaying of the animals is baptism, in which the old man dies. The great stone upon which the slaying was done is faith, without which the old man does not die. The slaughtering on the ground is the baptism of the heretics, whose blood they eat when they gather to themselves those washed without purification of sins. These animals taken from the Philistines signify either those brought back from the heretics or those converted from the Gentile world: the former the unskilled rebaptize, the latter they baptize otherwise than the Church hands down. Christ, as Saul, commanded that these, as oxen and sheep, be slain in his faith as upon a great stone, that is, that [men] of different kinds be baptized.

12_marg642: Because [he did it] obediently and rightly. But above, when he was rebuked by Samuel, he is not said to have built [an altar] to the Lord, because he built it disobediently.
12_marg643: BRING HITHER ALL THE CORNERS etc. He calls the princes the corners of the people, to whom the peoples on either side clung as walls to corners.
12_marg644: An oath of the Hebrews, which is understood by the contrary. As if he should say: let the evil that is due to thee be imputed [to me] if I do not kill thee.
12_marg645: WHO HATH WROUGHT [THIS GREAT] SALVATION etc. Good deeds done in the past profit much; for unless his past good deeds had helped Jonathan, he would not have escaped the evils hanging over him. For God is not unjust, that he should forget good deeds.
12_marg646: OX AND SHEEP etc. The Lord commands the beasts of Amalec to be destroyed for this reason: that there be no memory of him even in his beasts. For the Lord had said that he would blot out the memory of Amalec from under heaven; and because his memory was not wholly blotted out, Saul sinned by disobedience. Of Amalec it is said in Deuteronomy that 'he slew the hindmost of the people of God, who sat down weary'. The Hebrews explain the weary as those unclean according to the law, remaining outside the camp; whose foreskins, as they hand down, they cut off and threw toward heaven in mockery of God.
12_marg647: SAUL SAID TO THE CINITE. The Cinite is Jethro himself, the kinsman of Moses, from whom were the Cinites who dwelt with Amalec. For they were kindred and had an inheritance in his land. The Cinite showed kindness to the children of Israel because he cherished Moses in the land of Madian and gave him counsel how he should govern the multitude of the people.

12_marg648: IT REPENTETH ME etc. GREGORY. By this rebuke the pride of the king is cast down, which every prelate can turn to his own correction. When Saul esteemed himself little in his own eyes, he was made head in the tribes of Israel. As if [to say]: when thou didst behold thyself little, I made thee great above the rest; but because thou beholdest thyself great, thou art esteemed little by me. Whereas David, when he despised the power of his kingdom by dancing before the ark of the Lord, said: "I will play, and I will make myself meaner than I have done: and I will be little in my own eyes." If, then, the saints, even when they do mighty things, think meanly of themselves, what will they say who swell without works of virtue? But any works whatever are nothing unless they are seasoned with humility. A wonderful action done with elation does not lift up but weighs down. For he who gathers virtues without humility carries dust in the wind; whence, while he is seen to carry something, he is the worse blinded. Let us not, then, look at those above whom we already are, but at those below whom we still are, that we may always ascend to greater things out of humility.
12_interl842: an arch where he might describe the triumph of his glory
12_marg649: WHEN THOU WAST A LITTLE ONE. GREGORY. He is little in his own eyes who, while he considers himself, weighs himself unequal to the merits of others. For he sees himself great who stretches himself above the merits of others. But Saul did not abide in the good he had begun, because he swelled with the pride of power. But David, always thinking humbly of himself, and setting himself after the same Saul by comparison, when he found a chance of striking him spared him, and humbly prostrated himself before the raging adversary, saying: "Whom dost thou pursue, O king of Israel, whom dost thou pursue? A dead dog and a living flea." Yet he had already been anointed king; he had already learned that, Saul being rejected, he was kept for the helm of the kingdom. Let those learn, then, how they ought to humble themselves to their neighbours who do not yet know in what place they are held with God, if the elect humble themselves to those whom they know they are already set before. And this is proper to the elect: to think of themselves below what they are. Whence: "If I was not humbly minded, but exalted my soul." And elsewhere: "Whosoever is a little one, let him come to me" etc. For he who does not think himself humble does not lay hold of the wisdom of God.
12_marg650: Saul at first saw himself little; but lifted up by power he no longer saw himself little; preferring himself by comparison with the rest, because he could do more, he esteemed himself great above all. But when little with himself, he was great with God; when great with himself, he was little with God. Whence: 'Have they made thee ruler? Be not lifted up, but be among them as one of them.'
12_interl843: he answered proudly; he added evil to evil, because he strove to defend his fault, and thereby heaped it up
12_marg651: OBEDIENCE IS BETTER etc. Because by victims another's flesh, but by obedience one's own will, is slain. So much the sooner, then, does each one appease God, the more he immolates himself with the sword of the precept, the pride of his own choice being repressed. And disobedience is called the sin of witchcraft, that the greatness of the virtue of obedience may be shown from the contrary. For if to resist is as the sin of witchcraft, and to refuse to obey as the crime of idolatry, obedience alone is that which possesses the merit of faith, without which anyone is convicted of unbelief. Whence Solomon: "An obedient man shall speak of victory." For while we humbly submit to another's voice, we overcome ourselves in the heart. But it is to be known that evil is never to be done through obedience; but sometimes the good which is being done ought to be left off. For the tree in paradise which God forbade to be touched was not evil; but that man, well created, might grow through the merit of obedience, it was fitting that he should forbid him even from a good thing. It is to be noted also what is said there: Of every tree of paradise thou shalt eat etc. For he who forbids those under him one good thing must grant many, lest the mind, repelled from all, perish as it were fasting. It is to be known also that obedience is sometimes nothing if it has something of its own; but sometimes it is very small if it has nothing of its own. For when a higher place is commanded, he empties the virtue of obedience for himself who still pants for it with his own desire. But when reproaches or insults are commanded, unless the mind desires this of itself, it lessens for itself the merit of obedience, because it comes down to this unwillingly. Hence Moses humbly refuses the princedom of the people; but Paul boldly says: "For I am ready not only to be bound, but to die also in Jerusalem."
12_marg652: I WILL NOT RETURN WITH THEE etc. Another edition: I will not return with thee, says Samuel, because thou hast despised the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath despised thee, that thou be not king over Israel. And Samuel turned his face to go away, and Saul took hold of the hem of his double cloak and tore it. And Samuel said to him: The Lord hath torn the kingdom of Israel from thy hand this day, and will give it to thy neighbour, good above thee; and Israel shall be divided in two, and he will not be turned nor will he repent; for he is not as a man that he should repent; [a man] threatens and does not abide [by it].
12_marg653: BUT HE LAID HOLD UPON THE SKIRT OF HIS MANTLE, AND IT RENT. As in the passion of the Lord the high priest rent his garment, so too Saul [rent] the garment of the prophet. For the rending done by both powers, namely the royal and the priestly, shows that the kingdom and priesthood of the Jews could not stand, because they would not receive the true king and priest, that is, Christ.
12_marg654: He to whom he said: The Lord despiseth thee, that thou be not king over Israel, and: The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thy hand this day, reigned forty years, namely as long as David too reigned; and he heard this in the first time of his reign. We understand, then, that it was said because none of his stock was to reign; and we look to the stock of David, from whom Christ was born according to the flesh. Saul is also a figure of the people of Israel, which was to lose the kingdom to Christ, who would reign spiritually through the New Testament; of whom it is said: "He will give it to thy neighbour, good" above thee, that is, better; or above thee because he is good; whence: Until I make thy enemies thy footstool, among whom is Israel too. From whom, as his persecutor, Christ took away the kingdom, although there was there also an Israel in which there was no guile, as it were the wheat of that chaff. For thence were the apostles, thence the martyrs, of whom the first was Stephen; thence the Churches magnifying God. Whence follows: and Israel shall be divided in two: namely into Israel hostile to Christ and Israel cleaving to Christ; into Israel belonging to the handmaid and Israel belonging to the free woman. These two were at first together, until the barren, made fruitful by grace, should cry: "Cast out the bondwoman and her son." Because of the sin of Solomon, indeed, in the reign of his son Roboam, Israel was divided in two, until that whole nation was overthrown by the Chaldeans. But what has this to do with Saul, since it should rather have been threatened to David himself, whose son Solomon was? Lastly, the Hebrew nation is not divided among itself, but scattered over the lands in the same error. But the division which God threatened, under the person of Saul, who bore the figure of that kingdom and people, to the same kingdom and people, is signified to be eternal and unchangeable by what is added: And he will not be turned, nor will he repent; for he is not as a man that he should repent; [a man] threatens and does not abide. For where it is read that he repents, a change of things is signified, the divine foreknowledge remaining unchangeably; where, then, he is said not to repent, it is understood that he does not change. For whoever have passed over or will pass over to Christ were not of them according to the foreknowledge of God, [though they were] according to the one and same nature of the human race.
12_marg655: HATH RENT. Although afterwards he reigned forty years; but then he merited that it be rent from his stock and handed to a better, that is, David; and from Saul, that is, the Jews, the kingdom is taken away and handed to Christ.

12_marg660: AN EVIL SPIRIT OF THE LORD etc. ISIDORE. So too was called the sleep of the Lord, which came upon the soldiers of Saul when David took away the spear and the cup from the head of the sleeper: not that the Lord himself slept, but because it had been poured in by his will, that no one might perceive the presence of David. The evil spirit of God, then, is so called, that is, the minister of God, to do in Saul what the judge of all decreed that he should suffer.
12_marg661: SKILFUL IN PLAYING ON THE HARP. David was learned in the songs of music. The reasonable and measured concord of different sounds signifies the unity of the Church, which resounds daily in various modes. David restrained the evil spirit with his harp: not that there was such power in the harp, but in the figure of the cross of Christ, which was borne by the wood and the stretching of the strings, which even then put the demons to flight. But tropologically we are instructed by this deed to have compassion on our neighbour. For often a proud rich man is to be appeased by the soothing of exhortation; because often hard wounds are softened by light fomentations, and the fury of the mad is brought back to health when the physician soothes them. David, taking up his harp, calmed the madness of Saul. By Saul the powerful, by David the life of the saints is signified. When, then, Saul is seized by the unclean spirit, his madness is tempered by David's singing; because, when the sense of the powerful is turned to fury through elation, it is fitting that it be called back to health of mind by the calmness of our speech, as by the sweetness of the harp.
12_marg662: SAUL WAS REFRESHED. For before he was vexed by the demon even to suffocation. Boethius relates that a certain philosopher by the touch of the harp drove a demon from a possessed body.
