12_marg670: FOR [ISRAEL] HAD PUT [THEMSELVES] IN ARRAY etc. The fight of the Philistines against Israel can be taken as the fight of the demons against the Church. And Goliath signifies the pride of the devil, which David, that is, Christ, laid low in single combat, and rescued the people of God. He slew the lion and the bear: namely the devil and Antichrist, the one now lying in wait secretly, the other afterwards raging openly. Pride provoked humility, the devil Christ. David received arms of war, which because of his age and small stature he could not carry, and cast them off. He took five stones from the river and put them in the shepherd's vessel. Armed with these he conquered. So Christ, in the time of the revelation of the New Testament, to insinuate and commend grace, laid aside the bodily sacraments of the law, which were not imposed on the Gentiles, which we read in the old law and do not observe, but understand to have been sent before and set for some signification: these he laid aside as burdens of the law, and he took the law itself. For the five stones signify the five books of Moses. He took five stones from the river, that is, from this world; for the mortal world flows away. The stones were, as it were, in the river among the first people; there they lay idle and profited nothing. The river passed over them; but David took grace, that the law might be useful, which cannot be fulfilled without grace. "For love is the fulfilling of the law." Because, then, grace makes the law to be fulfilled: for grace is signified by milk. For this is what is free in the flesh, where the mother seeks not to receive but to give; she gives freely and is saddened if there be lacking one to receive. David showed that the law cannot work without grace when, wishing to join those five stones, by which the law in five books is signified, to grace, he put them in the shepherd's vessel in which milk used to be drawn. Armed with these he went forth against the proud one. He took one stone and cast one: he struck him in the forehead, and he fell, [struck] in that place of the body where he did not have the sign of Christ. He took five, he sent one: five books were chosen, but unity conquers. "Love, then, is the fulfilling of the law," as the Apostle says: Supporting one another in charity, careful to keep the unity of the spirit in the bond of peace. When he had laid him low, he took away his sword and cut off his head. Christ slew the devil with his own members, when the magi believed, whom he held in his hand and by whom he slaughtered others, turning their tongues against the devil; and so Goliath's head is cut off with his own sword.
12_marg671: I KNOW THY PRIDE. He thought there was swelling in him because of Samuel's anointing, as though he had taken boldness from it; and he feared lest, if he engaged with the Philistine, he should be killed. Whence he adds: thou art come down to see the battle; that is, in this thou appearest proud, that though thou hast no custom of fighting, thou inquirest into the deeds of battle as a soldier.
12_marg672: IS THERE NOT CAUSE TO SPEAK. As if he should say: there is, because it is not a wish to fight, but that I may know what I did not know. Yet he had taken boldness from this, that he had received the Holy Ghost, having experienced God's help in the lion and the bear; and therefore he boldly offered himself for single combat, not so much desirous of victory as an avenger of the blasphemies against God and the injuries to the people.

12_marg673: AND THE PHILISTINE CAME ON etc. AGAINST DAVID etc. Allegorically: the Philistines are the demons; Goliath is their head, who before the coming of the true David could not be overcome. Geth, the city of Goliath, is interpreted winepress: this is the world, or hell, in which, as in a winepress, he will trample those bound by sins; who, having left the heavenly rest, as it were of the seventh [day], fell into this world made in six days. The height of Goliath is the pride of the devil, through which he obtained princedom over the children of pride, lifting himself up like a palm. The arms of Goliath are the devil's cunning for doing harm. David was sent by his father to visit his brethren, and Christ by God the Father to the sheep that were lost of the house of Israel. David brought to his brethren an ephi of frumenty, that is, a measure of three bushels, and Christ commended the mystery of the Holy Trinity to believers. David brought ten little cheeses to the tribune, and Christ delivered the decalogue to the Jews. Eliab: my God father: the Jews, falsely claiming to have God as father, who, envying Christ, lost the birthright. The staff of David, the cross of Christ. Goliath, struck in the forehead, falls and is put under David himself; and the devil is struck in the forehead of his own when the sign of the cross is fixed in that place, and he is subjected in the members to Christ. David brought Goliath's sword to Jerusalem, and Christ transferred those whom he snatched from the devil's power into the Church for its defence. Saul inquires about the house of David and about him as though unknown, though David had long been attending him; and the Jews knew that Christ would come, and him whom in his bodily presence they could approve as the Son of God by his mighty works, as though ignorant, they say: Who art thou? And where is thy father?
12_marg674: Morally: when the members of the true David overcome the proud heretics, who bring forward the sentences of sacred Scripture, by those same sentences which they bring forward, they as it were behead the lofty Goliath with his own sword.

12_marg679: AND JONATHAN LOVED HIM. Jonathan, a warlike man, loved David, a youth fit for battles. 12_marg684: AND SAUL SAID: I WILL GIVE etc. ISIDORE. Saul, a cunning dissembler, sought to bind David to Michol his daughter if he would offer him a hundred foreskins of the Allophyli; but he offered two hundred. And so Saul, while he exposed him to danger, glorified him the more. So the Jews, while they strove against the will of God to kill Christ, wrought the salvation of the Gentiles. David first brought the foreskins of the foreigners, and so received Saul's daughter as wife; and Christ did not take the Synagogue before he had become glorious among the Gentiles. For he first cut away among the nations the pollution of the flesh, and afterwards was joined to the Synagogue. "For when the fulness of the Gentiles shall come in, then all Israel shall be saved." And he offered double foreskins for the Jews and the Gentiles, namely those gained; or because the number of believing Gentiles is greater than that of the Jews. The hatred of Saul against David grew so much that, as David played according to custom for his relief, he tried to pierce him with a javelin. By Saul the elation of the Jews, by David the humility of Christ is signified. When, then, Saul is seized by the unclean spirit, his madness is tempered by David's singing; because, when the sense of the Jews is turned to fury through blasphemy, it is fitting that it be called back to health by the calm of evangelical speech, as by the sweetness of the harp.

12_marg690: HE SENT MESSENGERS etc. WENT ALSO HIMSELF. RABANUS. Saul too and his messengers signify the Jews, who, while they desire to oppose Christ, have in their mouth the sacraments of the law and the prophets as testimony to Christ, and dispute with the Church as with prophets about the Scriptures, as those prophesied with the prophets.
12_marg691: HE PROPHESIED. These prophets were religious men called Nazarenes, who did not drink wine and were always free for singing hymns and psalms.
12_marg692: NAKED. The Jews too, stripped of faith and priesthood and kingdom, have the law and the prophets in their mouth.
12_marg693: WHAT! IS SAUL TOO etc. That is called a proverb which is often turned over in the mouths of speakers. For it seemed a wonderful thing that so profane a man should prophesy. And we too, when we see the unlearned teaching, rightly say: Is Saul too among the prophets?
12_marg694: RABANUS. A great question arises here: since in what precedes it is read, and Samuel saw Saul no more until the day of his death, how is he said here to have prophesied before Samuel? Which the Hebrews solve in two ways: namely that Samuel hid himself, that he might not be seen by him. Or he did not see him, namely clothed in the royal attire with which he was clothed, when it was said, he saw him not until the day of his death; and so he did not see him clothed, namely, in royal attire. And that he stripped himself is to be understood not of all his garments but only of the royal ones.
12_marg695: RABANUS. Again it is asked how those who had been sent to seize a man and lead him to death merited to be partakers of the prophetic spirit; and likewise Saul himself, seeking innocent blood? But Balaam too prophesied, and many will say in that day: "Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name" etc. To whom it will be said: "I never knew you: depart from me, you that work iniquity." It is not wonderful, then, that a reprobate man prophesied for a passing moment. But mystically Saul and his messengers signify the heretics, who have something of the spiritual gifts, as the testaments of the law and the gospel, and baptism. Which, when they come to the Church, is not to be violated in them, or given as though they did not have it; but they must acknowledge the unity in the bond of peace, without which, whatever they have, though it be holy and venerable, yet they themselves are the more unworthy the less well they have used those gifts.

12_marg697: AND THE LORD REQUIRED IT AT THE HAND. It is prolepsis, that is, anticipation; for this was done long after, when, Saul having been slain, the kingdom was transferred to the house of David, and those who had persecuted the innocent were punished by God. Then the Lord required it at the hand of the enemies, namely why they afflicted a holy man. Then they were compelled to render account, because they had hated him so long a time. Which can be understood of Absalom and of Seba the son of Bochri, of Saul and of the other enemies of David. Or the Lord required at the hand [of the enemies], that is, of David['s], why they too were not willing to enter into a covenant of peace with him with whom they saw the Lord to be. And Scripture anticipated these things in order to prove true what it had said, when the Lord shall have rooted out the enemies of David: namely that the enemies of David were rooted out from the earth, not by David avenging himself, but by the Lord avenging him.

12_marg700: FETCH ME THE ARROWS WHICH I SHOOT. What is it that Jonathan, wishing to save David while he lay hidden in the field beside the stone, shot two arrows as a sign, which a little boy, not knowing what he was doing, gathered and brought back into the city, except that the Father had hidden in the letter of the law, the Jews not knowing it, his only-begotten Son, to be sent for the salvation of the human race? David, then, was hidden in the field, and Christ in the world: "He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not." He sat beside the stone, because he was written in the tables of the law. Whence: "The Lord thy God is one" and: "Thou shalt not take the name of thy God in vain." Saul at the feast judged him to be a son of death, and Jewish perfidy at the paschal feast treated of the death of the Lord. When, then, the morning had dawned, Jonathan came into the field according to the appointment with David, and a little boy with him; he shot one arrow and shot another; and God the Father, as the morning of faith dawned, first brought forth the testimony of the law concerning Christ, then sent the prophets. Jonathan's boy gathered the arrows and brought them to his master, not knowing what he was doing. So the Jewish people, carrying the books of the law and the prophets, honoured them as divinely written, but knew not him whom Moses and the prophets had foretold.

12_marg703: THE PRIEST THEREFORE GAVE THEM. 12_marg704: WITHIN THE TABERNACLE. RABANUS. In the Hebrew: bound before the Lord. For perhaps he had vowed that he would stay some days in the tabernacle of the Lord and be free for prayers.
12_marg705: DOEG, AN EDOMITE. RABANUS. He was keeper of the camels, that is, of an unfruitful and crooked flock, and he is interpreted 'movement' or 'anxious'; who also struck Achimelech the high priest, who is interpreted 'my brother king'. By name and deed he signifies Judas, through whom the devil wrought fraud against Christ the true king, that, he being destroyed, the Church too might suffer, and the disciples of Christ and the priests be slain for his name. But in the house of Achimelech Abiathar alone, the chief of the priests, escaped; because no one can harm Christ, the prince of priests, who ascended victorious into heaven.
12_marg706: BUT DAVID LAID UP. ISIDORE. RABANUS. Achis is interpreted 'how is it?', by which ignorance is signified. For it is the word of one swearing and not acknowledging. Which was fulfilled in the Jews, who, when they saw Christ, did not acknowledge him. Before them he changed his countenance and went away. For there were there the carnal precepts of the law, there was the sacrifice according to Aaron; but he instituted from his body and blood the sacrifice "according to the order of Melchisedech." He changed his countenance in the priesthood, he changed it in the precepts, giving another testament, carnal working being made void. He slipped down between their hands when they seized and crucified him. And he stumbled against the doors of the gate, that is, he humbled himself to the beginning of our faith: the door of the gate is the beginning of faith; from faith the Church begins and reaches even to hope. That the spittle ran down upon his beard as of a madman, the Apostle discloses, saying: "We preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews indeed a stumblingblock, and unto the Gentiles foolishness." For spittle signifies weakness, because: "The foolishness of God is wiser than men." The spittle flows down the beard; for as weakness is shown in spittle, so strength is shown in the beard. He covered, then, his strength with the body of his weakness; and what was weak outwardly appeared as spittle, while the divine strength lay hidden within as the beard.

12_marg707: AND WHEN [THEY] HAD HEARD OF IT. RABANUS. 12_marg712: AND THERE WAS A CAVE etc. RABANUS. The king, caught by an unforeseen ambush in what he was contriving against the innocent, fell into the pit which he had made. But David, returning good for evil, did not kill him, but as testimony of the deed cut off the hem of his robe, though it would have been easier to destroy his adversary than to deceive him. David hid in the cave that he might not be found. And he who hides in a cave is covered with earth, that is, with flesh. And Jesus lay hidden in the flesh which he had received from the earth, that his divinity might not be found by the Jews: "For if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory." They, then, not knowing God, persecuted the man. Christ fled into the cave from the face of Saul; for so long did the Jews persecute him, until he was laid in the monument which was hewn in a rock. Saul goes into the cave to purge his belly, because the Jews sent forth the malice they had conceived against Christ as a foul odour, and showed their evil thoughts by worse deeds. David chose to save Saul rather than destroy him, whom, hidden in the cave, he had in his power, by Saul's own testimony. So too Christ, when he was in the cave of the flesh, had the persecuting people in his power, and did not kill them, of whom it was written: Slay them not. He silently cut off the edge of the robe, because Christ did not kill the Jews but took away the glory of the kingdom. 12_marg713: SAUL. GREGORY. Morally. What is signified by Saul but bad rulers? What by David but good subjects? For Saul to purge his belly is for wicked superiors to extend the malice conceived in the heart even to works of wretched odour, and to show the harmful things thought within by carrying them out in outward deeds. Yet David feared to strike him; because the minds of pious subjects, keeping themselves from every plague of detraction, strike the life of their superiors with no sword of the tongue, even when they rebuke their imperfection. For if at times through weakness they can scarcely refrain from speaking of some extreme and outward evils of their superiors, yet they speak humbly, and as it were silently cut off the hem of the robe; because, while they disparage the dignity set over them, though harmlessly and secretly, they as it were soil the garment of the king set over them; but yet they return to themselves and reprove themselves for the slightest laceration by word. For David's heart struck him because he had cut off the hem of Saul's robe. For the deeds of a superior are not to be struck with the sword of the mouth, even when they seem rightly to deserve rebuke. But if at any time the tongue slips against them even in the least things, it must be checked by the affliction of penance, that it may return to itself, and, when it has offended against the dignity set over it, may dread the judgment against itself of him who set that superior over it. For when we offend against superiors, we oppose the ordinance of him who set them over us. Whence Moses, when he knew that the people complained against himself and Aaron, said: "For what are we? Your murmuring is not against us, but against God."

12_marg718: THE SOUL OF MY LORD SHALL BE etc. By a most beautiful comparison she distinguished the state of the just and of the reprobate: the souls of the former she calls living, those of the latter seized by spiritual death. "For the soul that sinneth, the same shall die." The former she likens to bundles, the latter to the stone of a sling. For a bundle is bound tight that it may be kept; a stone is put in a sling that it may be cast away. So the elect are bound tight by the pressures of tribulations, that, admonished by them, they may be knit more closely to one another by mutual charity, and, united by the hands of the Redeemer, may be kept for ever. The reprobate, the more widely they are let go in their pleasures, the farther they are cast from the glory of the divine vision: "For they are cast off from the hand of God." And wonderfully does she describe the almighty providence of the heavenly protector, when she says that the soul of the holy man is kept with him as in the bundle of the living. For as it is easy for anyone to keep a bundle of grass or hay held in the hand, so is the power of our Saviour [able] to keep and guard the elect from the beginning to the end. Whence: "And no man shall pluck them out of my hand." And as a bundle is bound, so the glory of the saints is bound tight by true charity and surrounded by divine protection. But literally, the soul of David, though many persecuted him, was always kept in the lot of the living; but his enemies, as a stone whirled in a sling, troubled with unstable motion, were taken away from their borders or from human affairs.

12_marg726: WHOM SHALL I BRING UP etc. AUGUSTINE, TO SIMPLICIAN. Thou askest whether an evil spirit could have raised up the soul of a just man, so that it should be seen and speak with Saul? Is it not more to be wondered at that he took up the Lord and set him on the pinnacle of the temple? However he did it, it was done; unless one should say that the devil had easier licence to take up the living Lord whence he would and to set him where he would than to raise up the spirit of Samuel. But if this does not disturb us, because the Lord willed and permitted it to be done without any diminution of his power and divinity, as he suffered himself to be crucified and killed by the Jews, it is not absurd to believe that by some dispensation it was permitted that, not by the mastery of magic art or power, but by a hidden dispensation which escaped the pythoness and Saul, the spirit of the just man should show itself to the sight of the king, to strike him with the divine sentence. Or the spirit of Samuel was not truly raised from his rest, but some phantasm and imaginary illusion made by the machinations of the devil, which the prophet [so the edition] calls Samuel, as images are wont to be called by the names of the things they represent, as a picture of Cicero or Sallust; as the cherubim over the ark of the testament, made of metal for the sake of signifying a great thing, were called cherubim, though the heavenly powers are those that are called cherubim. Also, when anyone sees a dream, he does not say, I saw an image of Augustine, but, I saw Augustine, although at the time when he saw such a thing Augustine did not know of it. Pharao too said that he had seen in his dreams ears of corn and kine, not images of ears or kine. Perhaps, then, an image of Samuel appeared through the feigned contrivances of him who "transformeth himself into an angel of light." But if it moves anyone how true things were foretold to Saul by an evil spirit, that too can seem wonderful, that the demons acknowledged Christ, whom the Jews did not acknowledge. For when God wills that even weak spirits should know some true things, temporal things only, pertaining to this mortality, it is easy and not unfitting that the Almighty and just, for the punishment of those to whom these things are foretold, that they may suffer the evil that threatens before it comes, should by the hidden ordering of his mysteries impart to such spirits something of divination, that they may foretell to men what they hear from the angels. But they hear only so much as the Lord, the governor of all, commands or allows. Whence also the spirit of python in the Acts of the Apostles bears witness to Paul and proclaims him an evangelist. Yet they mingle deceits, and pronounce the truth with the aim not of teaching but of deceiving. Hence perhaps that image said that Saul would be with him, which is false; for between the good and the wicked after death a great chaos is fixed. Or it said, thou shalt be with me, for this reason: that it might be referred to the like condition of death, because each was a man and could die; already dead, he foretold death to the living.

12_marg728: THE AMALECITES HAD MADE AN INVASION etc. GREGORY. It is to be considered what it means that the Amalecites invade Siceleg and take booty. The Amalecites are called a licking people, by whom the minds of worldly men are designated, which, by coveting earthly things, as it were lick them while they delight in them. The licking people takes booty, as it were, when those who love earthly things heap up gains for themselves from the losses of others. And they do this while David is absent, because they neglect to have the Redeemer before the eyes of the heart. The Egyptian boy grows weary on the way, because the lover of the present world, covered with the blackness of sin, is often left by that same world weak and despised, so that he cannot run with it, but, broken by adversity, grows torpid. Him David finds, because Christ, truly strong of hand, turns to his love those whom he finds despised by the glory of the world. He feeds him with food, because he refreshes him with the knowledge of the word, because he makes him even his preacher. And because he could not follow the Amalecite, he becomes the guide of David, because he whom the world has deserted not only receives God in his converted mind, but by preaching leads him even into the hearts of others. With him as guide David finds the Amalecite feasting and destroys him, because Christ, through the preaching of those whom the world disdained to have as companions, destroys the gladness of the world.
